text: The hand-over of a signed offer is one element, SignedOfferHandover, returned as the result of the signed branch of TreatmentWorkflow, with the eleven properties treatmentId, caseId, treatmentType, signatureStatus, signedAt, validUntil, offerAmount, toState, paymentInstructionRequired, ruleId and ruleVersion. Six map to treatment fields of TSD S2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-001, DF-TRT-002, DF-TRT-004, DF-TRT-030, DF-TRT-010, DF-TRT-007) and five are request-context facts recorded on the decision record, with no column in rwb_treatment.
why: No source defines a hand-over element, a result type or a signature path; TSD S2 T3.1 carries signature_status and no signed-at, route, instruction or rule-version column; and the legacy story moved one case status in one schema, so its shape was never written down.
read: Legacy RWB-E3-008 sections 7, 11 and 14; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2.1 and T-A.1; FSD S2 v4 A2.8.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16 and R-SET-10; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and DP-13
applied_in: RWB-S2-E3008-APP and RWB-S2-E3008-CON: section 3, section 7 AC1 to AC4, section 9, section 11, section 12.5, section 12.7, section 13
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-treatment tech lead and the P3 case-workflow owner at the wave 2 contract freeze
impact: If the operations step needs a second element of its own, one element is added and the branch returns both; the properties, the rules and the criteria do not change.

text: The verified signature reaches the signed branch on the CUSTOMER_SIGNED case event that the parent CaseWorkflow forwards as a signal, carrying signed = Y or N, the verification flag and the signature time; the e-signature execution and its verification are P5 rwb-document's activity and the wave 2 integration harness proves the live path, so this story adds no contract dependency of its own. The signature is kept as signature_status (SIGNED on this path) and no signed-at column is created.
why: The legacy systems column names EasyApp e-signature, TSD T5.2.2 names contract generation and e-signature as a Temporal activity of P5, the FSD trigger line allows an event, a batch or a timer, and the Work Package fixes the contract dependencies of both stories as None.

applied_in: RWB-S2-E3008-APP: section 3, section 4, section 7 AC2, section 8 BR4, section 11, section 12.5, section 12.8; RWB-S2-E3008-CON: section 3, section 12.5
confirm: rwb-document owner with the rwb-case owner of the case router and the rwb-treatment tech lead at the wave 2 build start
impact: If the signature arrives as a P5 activity answer instead, the stage waits on the activity rather than on the signal and one fixture changes; the property set, the record and the criteria stay as written.

text: The case status, the operations (booking) queue and the one-working-day follow-up stay rwb-case's. The signed branch returns the hand-over and the parent CaseWorkflow applies WITH_OPS_BOOKING or WITH_OPS_SETTLEMENT, places the case in the operations queue and starts the task timer; rwb-treatment reads no case table and writes no case state.
why: Both rules of the legacy story move recovery_case.status inside one schema, while the target gives the case, its state, queues, tasks and timers to rwb-case, and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables; no contract states how a stage hands a case to the operations queue.

confirm: P3 owner of the case workflow with the rwb-treatment tech lead at the wave 2 build start
impact: If the parent does not own the transition, the stage would signal rwb-case over REST and a contract dependency would appear on the hand-over; no rule and no criterion changes either way.

text: The settlement instruction that R-SET-10 raises is carried as the paymentInstructionRequired flag, and the amount as offerAmount, on the hand-over element; rwb-payment (P8) raises the instruction and the partner side (S9) holds any instruction record, when the settlement is booked under R-SET-13. rwb-treatment writes no instruction row, the legacy partner_instruction table is S9's, and the live instruction path is proven by the wave 2 integration harness.
why: The legacy data table names partner_instruction, which the Ownership Map gives to S9, the TSD T5.2.2 lists only postProceeds of P8 and no published operation raises an instruction, and AC3 requires the instruction to be raised without naming its carrier.
